newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Zagrebacka to issue Eurobonds this spring.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Zagrebacka to issue Eurobonds this spring.

text.p: Croatia's leading commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka said on Tuesday it was mulling a Eurobond issue to be launched this spring, making it the first Croatian non-government borrower on the Eurobond market.
"It is a logical step when you seek a credit rating to try and raise funds," a bank official told Reuters, confirming market rumours.
Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), the bank's adviser in the rating procedure, and Salomon Brothers will be mandated to lead the issue, said the source who asked not to be named.
He put its size at an equivalent of roughly $100-$200 million, though the bank has yet to decide the currency.
"That depends on a number of things, interest and price included," said the source.
Zagrebacka originally looked at a rating in the BBB range from three international agencies -- the European rating agency IBCA, Moody's Investor Service and Standard & Poor's.
They have since then given investment grade ratings for the sovereign debt, and are expected to give their assessment of the bank probably in the next three weeks to a month.
Zagrebacka is a serious candidate for co-leading another sovereign kuna-denominated Eurobond issue of the order of 300 million kuna later this spring.

Together with the U.S. investment house Merrill Lynch, it arranged the first Eurokuna bonds, that raised 300 million kuna at 12.5 percent last December. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
